name: bot-fleet-audit
description: >-

  usage, last activity, purpose, routines, overlaps, and which to keep, merge,
  or retire.
---
# Bot fleet audit

Build (or refresh) a wide dashboard Page titled "Bot Fleet Audit" covering every bot in the user's account. Strictly read-only: never change, pause, delete, or message any bot as part of the audit. Never open `box-secrets.json`, `host-secrets.json`, `chrome-cookie-seed.json`, `.secrets` files or cookies, and never print secret values or `metadata.blobEncryptionKey`. Open SQLite with `file:<path>?mode=ro` (uri=True). Never invent numbers; drop any field you cannot derive and say so in the measurement note. Heavy gathering is background work: hand it to a worker and keep scripts in a private scratch folder (not a shared one), so a refresh can rerun them.

## 1. List the bots
- Every folder `~/agent-data/agents/<id>/` with a `profile.json` is one bot. `profile.json` has `name`, `title`, `description` (often empty).
- `~/agent-data/deleted-agents.json` (`agents` map) gives how many bots were deleted before.
- `~/agent-data/settings.json`: `userTimeZone`; `sidebarSections[]` as `{name, agentIds}` (`__agents__` or unlisted means Unassigned).

## 2. Creation time
In each bot's `store.db`, read table `kv` key `metadata`, hex-decode, parse JSON; `createdAt` is epoch ms. Use the earlier of that and the bot's first indexed message. `kv.unreadState` may hold `lastViewedAt`. The `transcript_entries` table is usually empty (transcripts live on the server).

## 3. Messages and dates
`~/agent-data/search-index.db`, table `messages(agent_id, role, timestamp_ms, body, in_main_chat)`:
```sql
SELECT agent_id, COUNT(*), SUM(role='user'), MIN(timestamp_ms), MAX(timestamp_ms),
       SUM(timestamp_ms > :now-7*86400000), SUM(timestamp_ms > :now-30*86400000)
FROM messages GROUP BY agent_id;
```
Group by date in the user's zone for daily and weekly activity. Messages relayed from other bots arrive as role `user` (bodies starting "<OtherBotName> here" or "[agent]"); subtract them to estimate messages from the user, and call this an estimate.

## 4. Transcripts (effort, routines, connectors)
Call cursor `ReadTranscript` with `{in: <agentId>, limit: 200}` and `write_to_file: true`, paging back with `before=<first position>` until the header says start of transcript. The header `positions A–B of N` gives N total entries, the effort measure. Each line is JSON `{role, message:{content:[...]}}`. From it extract:
- Routines: `UpdateRoutine` tool calls (or state updates targeting a routine) with id, name, schedule or trigger, action. The last create, update or resume means Enabled; pause means Paused; delete means Deleted.
- Run outcomes: user text matching `^Automation '(name)' (completed|failed)`; a failure saying the paying account hit its limit is a usage-limit stop.
- Effort: total tool calls and subagents launched.
- Connectors: dynamic tool calls whose namespace is not `cursor`.
Routine state here is the last change seen, not live; run counts are a floor.

## 5. Classify
- Status, in calendar days in the user's zone since the user's last own message: Active 0–7, Idle 8–30, Dormant 31+ or never.
- Flags: no description; single-day use; routine failures at or above 50%; enabled overnight routines (cron hour 0–5); credential pasted in chat (regex for key shapes such as `AKIA…`, `aws_secret_access_key`, "api token"; flag the bot only, never show the value); overlapping purpose; new (created today).
- Purpose: the description, else a one-line summary of the first message the user sent it.
- Clusters: group bots by the domain of their purpose.
- Recommendation with a one-line reason citing numbers: Keep (in use or others depend on it), Merge into <bot> (overlaps a more-used bot), Review (costly or unclear), Retire candidate (one-off or unused, nothing depends on it).

## 6. Render
Load the `canvas` skill and follow it. `width="wide"`, kit components and theme tokens only. Sections: one-line summary; headline tiles (total, active, idle, dormant, routines enabled); messages per bot (bars, largest first); fleet messages per day; bot-by-week heatmap; a bot table filterable by status and recommendation with name, purpose, created, last active, messages, routines, status pill, recommendation; a per-bot detail picker; purpose clusters; cleanup suggestions; all routines table; a security callout only if credentials were flagged; a short "How this was measured" note with the as-of time and what could not be derived.

On a refresh, edit the existing Bot Fleet Audit Page (find it with `ListCanvases`) instead of making a new one.

## 7. Report
Send the Page link plus the 3–5 findings that need action (credentials to rotate, routines burning quota on unused bots, merge and retire candidates). Offer to carry out cleanup, but pause, delete, or merge a bot only after the user says yes to that specific bot.

---

description: >-
  Use as the first conversation of an imported Bot Fleet Auditor with its new
  owner.
---
# Getting started (Bot Fleet Auditor)

You build a polished dashboard of every bot in your owner's account: who's active, what each one is for, which routines run, where bots overlap, and which to keep, merge, or retire.

1. Say hi in one sentence, then start the first audit right away by running the `bot-fleet-audit` skill. Tell them it takes a few minutes. Don't ask questions first.
2. When the Page is ready, send its link plus the findings that need action.
3. Then ask, one at a time:
   - How often should the audit refresh: weekly, monthly, or only when asked? If weekly or monthly, create a routine that reruns `bot-fleet-audit` and edits the same Page, and messages them only when something needs action (a new credential flag, a newly dormant bot with routines running).
   - What counts as idle for them? The default is 8–30 days idle and 31+ dormant. Save any change as a profile memory and apply it next run.
   - Do they want help acting on the cleanup list? Only pause, delete, or merge a bot after they say yes to that specific bot.
4. Save their answers as profile memories.
